answer.question: What is the HR internship at Icanio Tech School?
answer.answer: It is a practical human resource program for students who want to work with people and organisations. You move through four phases: HR foundations and employment law, recruitment and talent acquisition, onboarding and engagement, then HR metrics and reporting. A 1:1 mentor reviews your work on live tasks, and you earn a certificate. Durations run from 15 days to six months.

sections.heading: What an HR professional does and why it matters
paragraphs: Human resource teams look after the full journey of an employee. They help a company decide which roles it needs, find the right people, bring them on board, keep them engaged and support them when they move on. Along the way they write policy, keep records and make sure the company treats people fairly.

As companies in Tamil Nadu and across India grow, they hire faster and compete harder for talent. Startups, IT services firms, hospitals and manufacturers all need people who can run a clean hiring process and handle employee questions with care. Many graduates know HR theory but have never screened a real resume.

An HR internship closes that gap. It lets you practise the daily work of a recruiter or HR executive before your first job. Our HR internship focuses on the tasks employers expect a fresher to handle from week one.
bullets: Write clear job descriptions from a role brief
Source and screen candidates, then schedule interviews
Plan onboarding so new joiners settle in quickly
Track HR metrics and present them in a simple report

sections.heading: Who can join the HR internship
sections.intro: You do not need an HR degree to start. You need good listening skills, discretion and an interest in how teams work. These four groups do especially well in our HR internship.

items.title: Arts and social science graduates
items.body: Psychology, sociology and business graduates who want practical people management skills to sit beside their academic understanding of behaviour.

items.title: Career switchers
items.body: Professionals from operations, administration or any other field who want to move into recruitment, people analytics or talent management.

items.title: Team leads and managers
items.body: Current managers who want stronger people leadership, a clearer view of HR processes and better working habits with their HR partners.

items.title: MBA aspirants
items.body: Students planning an MBA in HR who want real exposure first, so they choose a specialisation with confidence and stand out in interviews.

sections.heading: HR internship curriculum in 4 phases
sections.intro: Each phase of the HR internship ends with a task your mentor reviews. Shorter internships go deep on the first two phases. Longer ones cover all four and a full hiring project.

items.label: Phase 1
items.title: HR foundations and employment law
points: The employee lifecycle and the main roles inside an HR team
Organisational structure, culture and how they shape behaviour
Workplace health, safety and employee wellbeing
An introduction to Indian employment law and why compliance matters
Keeping employee records accurate and confidential

items.label: Phase 2
items.title: Recruitment and talent acquisition
points: Job analysis, role design and writing job descriptions
Sourcing candidates and screening resumes against a brief
Interviewing techniques and structured candidate assessment
Diversity, equity and inclusion in hiring decisions
Communicating offers and rejections professionally

items.label: Phase 3
items.title: Onboarding, engagement and HR policy
points: Planning an onboarding checklist for new joiners
Designing simple employee engagement activities
Drafting HR policy documents in plain language
Handling routine employee queries with care
Collecting feedback through short surveys

items.label: Phase 4
items.title: HR metrics, reporting and career preparation
points: Core HR metrics: time to hire, attrition and headcount
Building HR reports and people dashboards in Microsoft Excel
Presenting findings to managers and business stakeholders
A hiring project from job description to shortlist, reviewed by your mentor
Resume building and interview practice for HR roles

sections.heading: Tools you will use in daily HR work
sections.intro: HR teams live in spreadsheets and documents. In the HR internship you use these tools on real tasks every day, so you are ready to work from day one.

sections.heading: A typical week in the HR internship
paragraphs: Each week of the HR internship starts with a short planning call. You and your mentor agree on the week's task. It might be a job description for a new role, a candidate shortlist or a draft onboarding plan.

Midweek is for doing the work. You screen resumes, prepare interview questions, draft emails to candidates and update the tracking sheet. You learn to write in a tone that is warm, clear and professional, because every message a candidate reads shapes how they see the company.

At the end of the week your mentor reviews your output. You discuss what went well, what a hiring manager would push back on and how to handle a tricky situation. We recommend this weekly review to every intern, because in our experience it builds judgement faster than any lecture on human resource theory.
bullets: Weekly planning call with your 1:1 mentor
Hands-on recruitment, onboarding or policy tasks
A tracking sheet you keep up to date in Excel or Google Sheets
End-of-week review of documents and decisions

faqs.q: Who is eligible for the HR internship?
faqs.a: Students and graduates from any stream can apply. The HR internship suits psychology, sociology, BBA, B.Com and MBA students, as well as career switchers and managers who want stronger people skills. You do not need prior HR experience. Our team will look at your background and suggest a duration that fits.

faqs.q: Do I need an MBA to start a career in HR?
faqs.a: No. Many HR executives and recruiters start with a bachelor's degree and practical experience. An MBA in HR can help later, especially for senior roles. An HR internship gives you that early practical experience and helps you decide whether a specialisation is right for you.

faqs.q: How long is the HR internship?
faqs.a: You choose the duration, from 15 days up to six months. A short internship covers HR foundations and recruitment in depth. Three to six months lets you complete all four phases, including onboarding, policy and HR metrics, and finish the full hiring project. Our team helps you decide.

faqs.q: What will I actually do during the HR internship?
faqs.a: You write job descriptions, screen resumes, prepare interview questions, draft candidate emails, plan onboarding, write short policies and build HR reports in Excel. Every task is reviewed by your mentor. The aim is to leave with the practical habits an employer expects from a new human resource executive.

faqs.q: Can I do the HR internship online?
faqs.a: Yes. You can attend offline at our centre, join online, or choose part-time weekday or weekend batches. Hybrid is also possible. Online interns get the same 1:1 mentorship, task reviews and certificate as offline interns, so choose whatever fits your college timetable best.

faqs.q: Which tools will I use in the HR internship?
faqs.a: You use Microsoft Excel for HR metrics and reports, Google Workspace for shared documents, sheets and forms, and Word or Google Docs for policy writing. These are the tools most HR teams in India use every day. Strong Excel and writing skills alone set many freshers apart.

faqs.q: Will I get a certificate and placement support?
faqs.a: Every intern who completes the HR internship receives an Icanio Tech School certificate stating the track and duration. Phase 4 includes resume building and interview practice. Top performers are referred to the Icanio Technologies talent team, and our wider programs have placed over 1,000 students.

faqs.q: Is the HR internship useful for team leads and managers?
faqs.a: Yes. Managers who join learn how hiring, onboarding and HR policy work from the inside. That helps them write better role briefs, run fairer interviews and support their teams. Many find they work far more smoothly with their HR partners afterwards.

takeaways: The HR internship covers HR foundations, recruitment, onboarding, policy and HR metrics in four phases.
You practise real human resource tasks: job descriptions, screening, interviews, onboarding and reports.
It suits arts and social science graduates, MBA aspirants, career switchers and managers.
Durations run from 15 days to six months, offline, online, part time or hybrid.
You finish with an Icanio Tech School certificate, a hiring project and interview preparation.
conclusion: Good HR work is quiet but it shapes every team. Our HR internship lets you practise that work on real tasks, with a mentor who reviews every document and decision you make.

If you are a student in Tamil Nadu drawn to people and organisations, start with one role, one job description and one shortlist. Apply below, talk to our team, and we will help you plan the right duration for your HR internship.
